# Metrics reference

Both processes serve Prometheus text on `GET /metrics` of their ops port. The controller replicas export the first group, the cache registry pod the second. Names are as scraped: counters end in `_total`.

The `namespace` and `pool` labels name a pool; they are empty when the pool is not yet known, for example after a failed TLS handshake. A label shown with a list of values takes only those values. Counters and histograms whose labels all have such lists, and the per-pool ones once the pool exists, start at 0 so that `rate()` and `increase()` see the first event. A label shown as `any` takes values that appear on use. No metric carries a per-allocation or per-pod label, so cardinality stays bounded by the number of pools.

## Controller metrics

| Name | Type | Labels | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `buildkit_leader` | gauge | none | 1 while this replica holds the leader Lease |
| `buildkit_leader_transitions_total` | counter | none | Times this replica gained or lost the Lease |
| `buildkit_watch_errors_total` | counter | `kind`: `pool`, `pod`, `claim`, `ca_secret`, `serving_secret`, `lease`, `controller` | Errors from a Kubernetes watch, by what it watches. The watch retries by itself |
| `buildkit_watch_namespace_unlisted` | gauge | `kind`: any; `namespace`: any | 1 while a pool or pod watch carries on without a namespace it cannot list |
| `buildkit_ca_valid` | gauge | none | 1 when the CA Secret loads and is usable. A CA whose notBefore is in the future still counts |
| `buildkit_cert_load_errors_total` | counter | `cert`: `ca`, `edge_serving` | Failures to load the CA bundle or the edge serving certificate |
| `buildkit_cert_not_after_seconds` | gauge | `kind`: `client_ca`, `internal_ca`, `edge_serving`, `edge_client` | Expiry (Unix seconds) of the client CA, the internal CA, and this replica's edge serving and edge client certificates. Worker certificates are per pod and have no series |
| `buildkit_releases_total` | counter | `namespace`; `pool`; `reason`: `released`, `allocation_idle`, `pod_lost`, `expired`, `failed`, `start_timeout`, `ca_replaced` | Worker pods retired after an allocation. `released`: the client or its claim ended it. `allocation_idle`: a delivered claim went unused for the pool's idle timeout. `pod_lost`: the pod was terminating when claimed. `expired`: the allocation TTL ran out. `failed`: the pod exited. `start_timeout`: the pod was not up within startTimeout. `ca_replaced`: a hard CA replacement made it unreachable |
| `buildkit_pool_pods` | gauge | `namespace`; `pool`; `state`: `warm`, `starting`, `allocated`, `draining` | Worker pods of a pool by state. `warm` are free and ready, `starting` are not ready yet, `allocated` are held by a client, `draining` are being deleted |
| `buildkit_pool_desired_warm` | gauge | `namespace`; `pool` | Free workers the pool is asked to keep now: scaling.minWarm, or the active schedule window's floor (status.desiredWarm) |
| `buildkit_pool_waiting` | gauge | `namespace`; `pool` | Claims waiting for a worker in the pool (status.waiting) |
| `buildkit_pool_max` | gauge | `namespace`; `pool` | The pool's worker ceiling (scaling.max) |
| `buildkit_pod_operations_total` | counter | `op`: `create`, `retire`, `delete`, `force_delete`; `result`: `ok`, `conflict`, `error` | Worker pod writes by the reconciler. `conflict` means the pod was already gone or replaced. `force_delete` is for a pod stuck draining |
| `buildkit_reconcile_total` | counter | `result`: `ok`, `error` | Pool reconcile passes. `error` when any step of the pass failed |
| `buildkit_reconcile_duration_seconds` | histogram | none | Duration of one pool reconcile pass |
| `buildkit_ca_replacements_total` | counter | `reason`: `missing`, `invalid`, `foreign`, `expired` | CA Secret creations and replacements by the leader. `missing`: created. `invalid`, `foreign` (not made by this install), `expired`: replaced after a backup |
| `buildkit_allocations_total` | counter | `namespace`; `pool`; `result`: `ok`, `invalid_request`, `unauthenticated`, `forbidden`, `pool_not_found`, `not_found`, `payload_too_large`, `unsupported_media_type`, `internal`, `pool_exhausted`, `pod_lost`, `not_ready`, `ca_unavailable`, `upstream_error` | Allocation outcomes. The API replica counts the requests it refuses, with the error code as `result`. The leader counts how each claim ends: `ok` when it binds, `pool_exhausted` at its queue timeout, and so on. A poll or a 202 counts nothing. `pool_not_found` carries empty namespace and pool |
| `buildkit_allocation_duration_seconds` | histogram | `namespace`; `pool`; `path`: `warm`, `cold` | Time from claim creation to bind, for claims that bound. `warm`: the leader bound it on its first look. `cold`: it waited for a worker |
| `buildkit_queue_wait_seconds` | histogram | `namespace`; `pool`; `result`: `ok`, `timeout` | Time a claim spent queued, from its creation. `ok`: it bound. `timeout`: it ran out of queue time |
| `buildkit_allocation_held_seconds` | histogram | `namespace`; `pool`; `reason`: `released`, `allocation_idle`, `pod_lost`, `expired`, `failed`, `start_timeout`, `ca_replaced` | How long a worker was held, from its bind to its retirement, by the same reasons as `buildkit_releases_total`. Use it to size scaling.max and the TTLs |
| `buildkit_claim_conflicts_total` | counter | `namespace`; `pool` | Claim patches the leader lost to another writer (HTTP 422, 409 or 404) |
| `buildkit_cache_allocations_total` | counter | `namespace`; `pool`; `tier`: `trusted`, `untrusted` | Claims that bound with cache flags, by cache tier |
| `buildkit_claims` | gauge | `phase`: `Pending`, `Bound`, `Expired`, `Lost`, `Failed` | BuildKitClaims in the leader's store by phase. Cleared when the leader's term ends |
| `buildkit_claim_reconciles_total` | counter | `result`: `failed`, `expired`, `lost`, `idle`, `abandoned`, `collected`, `released` | What the leader's tidy pass did to claims. `failed`: a claim from a namespace it does not serve. `expired`: a bound claim's TTL ran out. `lost`: its worker went away. `idle`: a delivered claim went unused. `abandoned`: a CI claim whose client is gone was deleted. `collected`: a finished CI claim was deleted. `released`: the worker of a gone or ended claim was retired |
| `buildkit_http_requests_total` | counter | `route`: `/v1/allocations`, `/v1/allocations/{id}`, `/v1/pools`, `/v1/tunnel`, `other`; `status`: any, starting with `200`, `201`, `202`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `409`, `429`, `503` | API requests by matched route template and HTTP status. `other` is any unmatched path |
| `buildkit_http_request_duration_seconds` | histogram | `route`: `/v1/allocations`, `/v1/allocations/{id}`, `/v1/pools`, `/v1/tunnel`, `other` | API request duration until the response head. A tunnel request ends when the tunnel closes |
| `buildkit_auth_total` | counter | `method`: `oidc`, `serviceaccount`; `result`: `ok`, `invalid`, `unknown_issuer`, `error` | Bearer token checks. `invalid`: bad or expired token. `unknown_issuer`: no configured issuer matches. `error`: the keys or the TokenReview call were unavailable |
| `buildkit_jwks_fetch_total` | counter | `issuer`: any; `result`: `ok`, `error` | Fetches of an OIDC issuer's signing keys, by configured issuer URL |
| `buildkit_edge_connections_total` | counter | `namespace`; `pool`; `result`: `ok`, `tls_error`, `bad_san`, `pod_not_found`, `alloc_mismatch`, `expired`, `pod_not_ready`, `store_stale`, `upstream_error`, `allocation_limit`, `namespace_limit`, `connection_limit`, `handshake_limit`, `peer_handshake_limit`; `transport`: `tcp`, `tunnel` | Client connections to the edge by outcome. `ok`: proxied. `tls_error`, `bad_san`: the client certificate was refused before an allocation was known (empty namespace and pool). `pod_not_found`, `alloc_mismatch`, `expired`, `pod_not_ready`: the allocation's pod or lease failed a check. `store_stale`: a pool or pod watch erred since its last completed list. `upstream_error`: the worker could not be reached. `allocation_limit`, `namespace_limit`, `connection_limit`: a connection cap. `handshake_limit`, `peer_handshake_limit`: an unfinished handshake was evicted by a newer one |
| `buildkit_edge_active_connections` | gauge | `namespace`; `pool`; `transport`: `tcp`, `tunnel` | Proxied connections open now |
| `buildkit_edge_handshake_seconds` | histogram | `transport`: `tcp`, `tunnel` | Client TLS handshake duration, including certificate verification |
| `buildkit_edge_upstream_connect_seconds` | histogram | `transport`: `tcp`, `tunnel` | Time from the end of the client handshake to the end of the upstream TLS handshake: the edge's own overhead |
| `buildkit_edge_bytes_total` | counter | `direction`: `client_to_worker`, `worker_to_client`; `transport`: `tcp`, `tunnel` | Bytes proxied between clients and workers |
| `buildkit_edge_revocations_total` | counter | `reason`: `released`, `expired`, `pod_gone`, `drain`; `transport`: `tcp`, `tunnel` | Live connections closed because their allocation ended. `released`: the pod's allocation changed. `expired`: the certificate's notAfter passed. `pod_gone`: the pod was deleted. `drain`: shutdown ran out of drain time |
| `buildkit_api_proxy_protocol_headers_total` | counter | `result`: `proxied`, `local`, `timeout`, `truncated`, `io_error`, `bad_signature`, `bad_version`, `bad_command`, `oversized`, `short`, `unsupported_family` | PROXY protocol v2 headers read on the API listener, one per connection from a trusted source. `proxied` and `local` were accepted; the rest are the reason the connection was closed |
| `buildkit_edge_proxy_protocol_headers_total` | counter | `result`: `proxied`, `local`, `timeout`, `truncated`, `io_error`, `bad_signature`, `bad_version`, `bad_command`, `oversized`, `short`, `unsupported_family` | PROXY protocol v2 headers read on the edge listener, one per connection from a trusted source. `proxied` and `local` were accepted; the rest are the reason the connection was closed |

## Cache registry metrics

| Name | Type | Labels | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `buildkit_watch_errors_total` | counter | `kind`: `pool`, `pod`, `claim`, `ca_secret`, `serving_secret`, `lease`, `controller` | Errors from a Kubernetes watch, by what it watches. The watch retries by itself |
| `buildkit_watch_namespace_unlisted` | gauge | `kind`: any; `namespace`: any | 1 while a pool or pod watch carries on without a namespace it cannot list |
| `buildkit_registry_requests_total` | counter | `route`: `base`, `blob`, `upload`, `manifest`, `other`; `method`: `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PATCH`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `other`; `status`: any | Registry requests by matched route, method and HTTP status. `other` is any unmatched path or method |
| `buildkit_registry_request_duration_seconds` | histogram | `route`: `base`, `blob`, `upload`, `manifest`, `other` | Registry request duration until the response head |
| `buildkit_registry_denied_total` | counter | `action`: `pull`, `push` | Requests refused by the worker's grant, by the action asked for. Denied `push` is expected for untrusted allocations |
| `buildkit_registry_connections_refused_total` | counter | `reason`: `tls_error`, `handshake_timeout`, `bad_certificate`, `client_auth_eku`, `bad_san` | Connections closed before a request: a failed or timed-out handshake, or a client certificate that names no worker |
| `buildkit_registry_received_bytes_total` | counter | none | Blob and manifest bytes received in pushes |
| `buildkit_registry_gc_evicted_manifests_total` | counter | `budget`: `pool`, `volume` | Manifests evicted by garbage collection to fit a budget: `pool` is a pool's share, `volume` is the whole store |
| `buildkit_registry_gc_deleted_blobs_total` | counter | none | Blobs deleted by garbage collection |
| `buildkit_registry_stored_bytes` | gauge | none | Bytes of blobs in the store. Compare it with the store budget (`--max-size`) |
| `buildkit_registry_blobs` | gauge | none | Blobs in the store |
| `buildkit_registry_manifests` | gauge | none | Manifests in the store, over all repositories |
| `buildkit_registry_store_operations_total` | counter | `op`: `get`, `put`, `put_part`, `complete`, `abort`, `delete`, `list`; `result`: `ok`, `error` | Calls to the store (the volume or a bucket), by kind and result. `put` counts the start of a multipart upload too; `delete` counts each key; `list` counts each listing. A `get` or `delete` of a missing key is `ok`: the end of a race with garbage collection |
| `buildkit_registry_store_operation_duration_seconds` | histogram | `op`: `get`, `put`, `put_part`, `complete`, `abort`, `delete`, `list` | Store call duration: a `get` until the response head, a `list` until its last page, a `delete` until that key's result |
